clue.text: Troops ordered to accept tackle

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered
rig means gear or tackle, as on a ship or for fishing

explanation.surface: Soldiers are commanded to take on board some equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' reads as describing the troops lining up, but it gives BADE, which takes in RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military unit made up of several battalions of soldiers.

clue.text: Getting to feeling pain again

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
aching means feeling pain

explanation.surface: Someone gets to the point of hurting once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' at the end goes first, as the prefix RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching a place is arriving at it, which is what getting to means.

clue.text: Present coverage in newspaper after US soldier stole

indicators.note: after puts the newspaper behind the soldier

parts.note: GI is a US soldier
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
a stole is a shawl, a wrap

explanation.surface: A newspaper report says an American soldier stole something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' reads as a verb but is the scarf, giving WRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Gift wrap is decorative paper covering a present.

clue.text: Record on order — keep being inconvenience!

indicators.note: on means placed next to, the record coming first

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
a keep is a castle's stronghold, a fort

explanation.surface: Having to store a record that has been ordered is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour; 'keep' is the castle tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Discomfort is unease or hardship, a noun synonym for inconvenience.

clue.text: In archipelago, big dry area

indicators.note: in means the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A large arid region in a group of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast desert in Mongolia and China, an example of a dry area.

clue.text: Barbarian in charge of architectural style

parts.note: the Goths were a Germanic people seen as barbarians by Rome

explanation.surface: A barbarian was put in control of a style of building.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is the medieval building style with pointed arches, named after the Goths.

clue.text: Case on which one takes a stand, so to speak

definitions.meaning: a box holding a bar of soap

definitions.text: on which one takes a stand, so to speak
definitions.meaning: a platform for an impromptu speech, the speaker standing on a crate

explanation.surface: A box that someone stands on to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a crate for soap; figuratively an improvised platform for airing views publicly.

clue.text: One looks down in the mouth when at work

definitions.text: One looks down in the mouth when at work

parts.words: One looks down in the mouth when at work
parts.note: down in the mouth means glum, but here it is literal: someone peering into a patient's mouth

explanation.surface: Someone who looks miserable on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional peers into patients' mouths to examine and treat teeth.

clue.text: Droning sound of instant message when holding on

parts.note: mo is a short moment, an instant

indicators.note: holding means one word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: a note is a short written message
taken as written

explanation.surface: Complaining about the boring hum of an instant message while you wait on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instant message' looks like one phrase, but the two words split and do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A monotone is a voice or noise that stays on one unvarying pitch, which is what droning means.

clue.text: Flashy fliers leading swimmers

indicators.note: leading means the first piece goes in front of the second

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's body of airmen
fish are creatures that swim

explanation.surface: Showy pilots heading a group of swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is the Royal Air Force, the UK's air arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish describes a showily disreputable, dashing style, close in sense to flashy.

clue.text: Most memorable experience could be Helvellyn

definitions.meaning: the best or most exciting moment of an event or period
Helvellyn is a mountain in England's Lake District, an elevated place, given as an example

explanation.surface: Climbing a famous fell might be the best part of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Helvellyn is one of the highest mountains in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the best moment of something, and literally a lofty location such as a summit.

clue.text: Take notice of circling scruff limiting parking, getting browbeaten

indicators.note: circling means surrounding the next part

parts.note: to heed is to take notice

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, holding something within bounds

parts.note: the scruff is the back of the neck

explanation.surface: Someone notices being grabbed by the scruff and parked, and feels bullied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' makes NPECK, and 'circling' wraps the noticing word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Henpecked means nagged and dominated, usually by a spouse, a close synonym of browbeaten.

clue.text: Article set out how to become famous rock group?

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article

indicators.note: set out means the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A magazine piece explains how to become a famous rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' reads as 'explained' but signals rearranging HOW.
explanation.definitionFit: This band was one of Britain's best-known rock groups of the 1960s and later, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Bill promises to pay after repair, being dishonest

indicators.note: after places the pieces that come first in the clue behind the repair word

parts.note: to mend is to repair
AC is short for account, a bill
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Someone swears they will settle the invoice once the repairs are done, and is lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacious is a formal synonym for lying or untruthful.

clue.text: Sweet wine — it'll be felt later on

parts.note: afters is British slang for a dessert or sweet course
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: A dessert wine whose effects come on later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet wine' looks like one item but splits: AFTERS is British for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftershock is a smaller tremor that follows an earthquake, felt after the main quake.

clue.text: Pavlova, perhaps, that gets sent back just the same

indicators.text: that gets sent back just the same
indicators.note: read backwards the name is unchanged, so it is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A meringue dessert returned to the kitchen exactly as served.
explanation.walkthrough: Pavlova looks like the dessert, but it is the ballerina Anna Pavlova; '?perhaps' marks her first name as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian ballerina Pavlova had this first name, so it is an example of a Pavlova's given name.

clue.text: Scheme news boss threw out

parts.note: a project is a planned scheme
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor rejected a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scheme' looks like the definition, but it is wordplay; the definition is 'threw out' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To project something is to throw or cast it forward, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Bring to light boat having stopped short abruptly in the middle

indicators.note: stopped short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a dredger is a boat that scoops silt

indicators.note: in the middle means take the central letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A boat halted suddenly, then revealed something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abruptly' looks like part of the story, but its middle two letters supply UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge something up is to reveal or uncover it, often something forgotten.

clue.text: Revolutionary test case for music-maker

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: A legal test case about a radical musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a tape of recorded sound, so it produces music when played.

clue.text: Having Elvis hairstyle, I will be knocked out by a drunk

indicators.note: knocked out by means one letter is replaced by another

parts.note: a quiff is the swept-up hairstyle Elvis Presley wore

explanation.surface: An Elvis lookalike gets knocked out by a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a drunk' looks like a person; 'a' replaces I and 'drunk' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaffed means drank heartily, matching drunk as a past participle.

clue.text: Unfavourable notice with few lines

parts.note: an ad is a notice advertising something
a verse is a few lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A bad review with just a handful of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means harmful or contrary, a synonym for unfavourable.

clue.text: Wander in said ancient city

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, giving one with the same sound

parts.note: Rome is the ancient capital of the Roman empire

explanation.surface: Wandering through a famous old city, as the saying goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to travel aimlessly, a synonym for wander.

clue.text: Person setting out on a task as mortician

definitions.text: Person setting out on a task
definitions.meaning: one who undertakes or takes on a job
an American word for a funeral director

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a job as a funeral director.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who takes on a task; in normal use, a funeral director who arranges burials.

clue.text: Run on guide to London or South — they're used for short cuts every morning

definitions.text: they're used for short cuts every morning

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the A-Z is a well-known street map of London
taken as written

explanation.surface: Taking a London street map south to find quick routes.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is a classic book of London street maps. 'short cuts' looks like quick routes; it is a close shave.
explanation.definitionFit: These blades are used in daily shaving, cutting stubble short.

clue.text: First to stand by unhappy person that loves being cruel

indicators.note: to stand by means to be placed next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: sad means unhappy
first is written 1st, and the figure 1 looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: A miserable person who enjoys cruelty is the first to stand by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' looks like 'first letter of', but it is 1ST, read as the letters IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist takes pleasure in inflicting pain or humiliation on others.

clue.text: Frantic having refined novel, penning the last character

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals
novel means new, so the letters are given a new order

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A writer is in a frenzy after polishing a novel and writing its final character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but signals rearranging REFINED to FRENIED, which is 'penning' Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied means wildly agitated and uncontrolled, a synonym for frantic.

clue.text: Italian 11 Across that erupts in Canterbury?

indicators.note: erupts means bursts upwards, so in a down clue the letters read from bottom to top
in means the letters lie within the word that follows

explanation.surface: An Italian volcano erupting in an English cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 Across is a lofty place; 'erupts' sends the letters hidden in Canterbury upward.
explanation.definitionFit: This active volcano in Sicily is an Italian mountain, a lofty peak.

clue.text: Need to have verse in poetry replaced

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word
replaced means the letters are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A poem needs a verse swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts V inside POETRY, and 'replaced' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Poverty is a state of want, a noun synonym for need.

clue.text: Preserve offered by inns here for spreading

indicators.note: spreading means the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Something conserved is offered by the local pubs here for spreading on bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for spreading' looks like jam on toast; 'spreading' rearranges INNS HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enshrine is to preserve something, often in law or custom, protecting it from change.

clue.text: Someone on boat beginning to sell fish

indicators.note: beginning to means take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: A boatman starts to sell some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the captain of a boat, so one person aboard.
